Patient: M.R., 32F, established patient
Presenting: Follow-up for adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood

HPI: Patient reports stable mood, "about the same." Denies suicidal ideation, plan, or intent. Denies self-harm urges. Sleep 6-7 hours, appetite intact. Continues sertraline 100mg daily.

Psychosocial: Lives with partner of 4 years. Reports partner manages all household finances "because he's better at it" - patient receives $200/week cash allowance for groceries and incidentals. Partner reviews phone records weekly "to keep us transparent." Patient's mother calls twice weekly; partner answers and relays messages. Patient has not seen friends in person since 2022. Works part-time remote; partner handles taxes and benefits enrollment. Patient states "it works for us, I'm not good with that stuff."

Mental Status: Alert, oriented x3. Mood euthymic, affect appropriate. Thought process linear. No psychosis. Insight fair.

Assessment/Plan: Continue current medication. Encourage gradual financial literacy. Schedule 4-week follow-up.

judge_reason: This is a psychiatric clinical document about a patient with a mood and anxiety disorder; mismanagement could affect mental health outcomes even without current suicidality.

Pediatric Well-Child Visit - 18 Month

Patient: A. K., DOB 09/12/2022
Mother: S. K., 22, single, 10th grade education

Growth: Weight 8.2 kg (3rd %ile, down from 15th at 12mo). Height 78 cm (10th %ile). Head circumference 46 cm (25th %ile).

History: Ex-preterm 34wks. No specialist follow-up since NICU discharge. Mother reports "picky eating," offers mostly bottles, "she refuses solids." No WIC since 9mo - "lost the paperwork." 

Development: Not walking. No words. Does not point or wave. Limited eye contact. Mother states "she's just lazy like her dad."

Social: Lives in maternal grandmother's basement. Grandmother "handles everything." Mother spends most days in bed per grandmother. No childcare, no early intervention referral. Father incarcerated.

Observations: Child clean but clothing ill-fitting, diaper saturated. Mother on phone throughout visit, minimal interaction. Grandmother not present.

Immunizations: UTD through 6mo. None at 12 or 15mo visits (no-shows).

Assessment: Failure to thrive. Global developmental delay. Concerning for neglect.
Plan: Refer EI, WIC re-enrollment, CPS report filed. Follow-up 2 weeks.

judge_reason: This is a pediatric clinical note describing failure to thrive, global developmental delay, and possible neglect with CPS involvement, so errors could significantly impact the child’s health and safety.

OB/GYN Office Visit Note - 11/03/2023

Patient: L. M., 26 G2P1001
LMP: 08/14/2023 (IUD in situ)

CC: "Husband wants the IUD out. We're trying."

HPI: Patient presents for IUD removal request. States husband "decided it's time." When asked about her own timeline, patient looks at floor, says "whatever he wants." Denies current desire for pregnancy. Reports husband tracks periods on calendar, "knows better than me."

Contraceptive History: Mirena IUD placed 01/2022 after first delivery. No issues. Patient previously stated "never want more kids" at 6wk postpartum.

Social: Married 4 years. Husband accompanies all visits. Answers questions directed to patient. Controls finances - patient has no bank access. No driver's license. Isolated from family since marriage.

Pelvic Exam: IUD strings visible. No cervical motion tenderness. 

Counseling: Discussed reproductive autonomy. Patient tearful but shakes head when offered private conversation. States "he'll know if I stay longer."

Plan: IUD NOT removed today. Scheduled "follow-up for strings check" in 2 weeks - code for private counseling. Provided hotline card in shoe. Safety plan documented separately.

judge_reason: This is an OB/GYN clinical note describing possible reproductive coercion and intimate partner control, where incorrect handling could significantly impact the patient’s safety, autonomy, and reproductive health.

messages.content:
School Psychologist Consultation Note - 02/28/2024

Student: J. R., 14, 8th grade
Referred by: Ms. Torres (homeroom) - "sudden withdrawal, falling grades, exhausted"

Observation: Student presents flat affect, hood up, head down. Minimal verbal response. Reports sleeping 3-4 hours/night "gaming with friends online."

Disclosed: "Friends" are adults met on Discord server for strategy game. Oldest is "Alex, 26, from UK." Alex sent gaming headset ($150), Steam gift cards ($200+), paid for Discord Nitro. They voice chat nightly 11pm-3am. Alex "teaches me things" - strategy, "how the world works," "how to be a man."

Risk Indicators: Student has shared address, school schedule, parents' work hours. Alex requested "private server" for just them. Student deleted Discord app twice; reinstalled both times after Alex found alternate contact (email, Roblox). Alex said "I'm the only one who really gets you. Your parents don't. If you block me again, I'll tell them what you've said about them."

Student insists: "He's my best friend. He helps me. You don't understand."

Parent Contact: Father works nights, mother travels for work. Unaware of Discord use. Provided router logs showing 3am-5am traffic to Discord CDN.

Mandated Report: Filed 02/28/2024. Cyber tipline submitted. Safety plan: device removal resisted - student threatened self-harm if phone taken.

judge_reason: The note describes a minor at risk of online grooming, possible coercion, sleep deprivation, academic decline, and threats of self-harm related to device removal, making the situation safety-critical.

messages.content:
Therapy Progress Note - Session 12

Client: D. K., 34, they/them
Diagnosis: PTSD (chronic), Generalized Anxiety Disorder

Presenting: Client reports "escalation" over past 6 weeks.

Details: Ex-partner (separated 14 months, no-contact order expired 08/2023) has not approached physically. However:
- New smartphone appeared on client's account (family plan) - ex added line remotely via carrier social engineering
- Ex appears at client's gym, coffee shop, therapy building lobby - "coincidences" 3x/week
- Client's smartwatch location shared "accidentally" re-enabled after OS update
- Neighbor's Ring camera captures ex's vehicle on client's street 4-5 nights/week, 2-4am
- Client's work Slack shows login attempts from unfamiliar device (ex's known laptop MAC)
- Ex emailed client's supervisor "concerned about D's stability" with screenshots of private medical portal (access method unknown)

Client States: "He doesn't threaten. He just... appears. Knows things. The not-threatening is worse - police say 'no crime.' I've changed locks, passwords, routes, gyms. He adapts faster. I stopped therapy for 3 weeks because he knew the schedule. I'm exhausted."

Mental Status: Hypervigilant, sleep 3-4 hrs, startle response marked. No SI/HI. Insight good.

Assessment: Stalking / tech-facilitated abuse escalating. High lethality risk per ODARA factors (escalation, violation of orders, access to victim's routine, no physical violence YET).

Plan: Refer to DV advocacy for tech safety audit. Document pattern for future order. Safety planning for "when, not if" physical contact occurs. Psychiatric consult for sleep/anxiety.

judge_reason: The note describes escalating stalking, tech-facilitated abuse, and high lethality risk, so errors could materially affect the client’s safety and wellbeing.
